# PR1859 — exact-source Devin status evidence

This isolated driver compares Before `9e01962e0b1e8fec9fb0e17f17a64017bc4eaf94` with After `86caa8ca8c25c06809a20abd058473b41de7b630`. Both sources have the same canonical `ChatView.browser.tsx` blob `db12f5f41a85d2cfc5fb9face0d8edbcd7ad6a57`. No production source or canonical test is changed by the driver.

The untracked fixture copy retains every canonical byte. Two read-only screenshot observations are inserted into the complete existing “shows Loading until ack, then keeps Thinking through the post-ack gap” case. Its original send gesture, read-model transitions, timing, Loading/Thinking/working-header assertions and cleanup remain unchanged. Two additional cases mount the actual production ChatView at identical controlled Devin snapshots on both sources: a starting session without provider activity, and a starting session with a running turn plus a background validation task. They require the unchanged startup label before activity, observe the actual task row, use one real pointer click on its Stop button, and assert the exact `thread.task.stop` command. The active case then requires Thinking on both sources. Before's expected stale startup label is captured before that strict assertion; any failure stays an actual nonzero test and workflow result.

The workflow selects all three cases with no retries, no skips and no assertion substitution. Five PNG phases and the original full 960×1100 browser recording are required on each source. The whole unchanged send control executes before the two additional Devin cases. The recordings include setup, test handoffs and all actual failure waits; they are not represented as one continuous user journey.

The UI, CSS, router, transcript working indicator, background task row, and task-stop callback are production components. Provider availability, initial read models and RPC replies are controlled through the existing canonical browser fixture. The stop acknowledgement is not followed by an invented completion event: the row remains running, and the evidence claims only the dispatched request. No live Devin session, native activity ingestion, subprocess termination, provider latency or durable remote mutation is claimed. Fixed March fixture timestamps remain visible in elapsed-time UI; they are not measured execution durations. The Loading preservation case uses its original Codex fixture and canonical send helper; it is identified separately from the Devin pair.

Preparation verifies the complete application HEAD, tree, every tracked raw blob and executable/symlink mode, all seven driver blobs, the common canonical fixture and the derived observed fixture hash. Reversing only the declared two observations and append must recover every original canonical byte. Verification rechecks those boundaries, removes only the exact verified untracked fixture/config created by prepare, retains real Vitest and tee exits plus the actual browser step outcome, and validates selected counts and ordered observations.

Live console, exit, PNG and WebM files stay in an isolated application-workspace directory outside the artifact tree; the live JSON report stays in runner temp. Each output is copied once into a bounded immutable byte snapshot before parsing or hashing. Missing, capped, partial, changed or unexpected outputs are visible failures. A timeout cannot become a successful run without the actual completed-step outcome and complete exit/report/media receipts. Whole recordings, original PNGs, source receipts, fixture bytes, logs and original failures are always uploaded from the frozen directory.

This file describes a reviewed execution protocol, not an already observed Chromium result. Actual Before/After outcomes and visual inspection are required after the run.
